entries.64.17: saluted Lakshmana and Bharata with joined palms, and the household priest Vasishtha, and that mighty one of composed spirit went round him and set out.
entries.64.18: Having sent his army before him, thronged with the finest elephants and horses, that increaser of the line of the Raghus waited a month beside the king, and then went on his way.
entries.65.1: Having sent forward his whole force and stayed a month upon the road, Shatrughna went on swiftly, alone.
entries.65.2: Halting two nights on the way, that brave delight of the Raghus came to the holy hermitage of Valmiki, that best of dwellings.
entries.65.3: Saluting that great-souled Valmiki, best of sages, he stood with joined palms and said:
entries.65.4: 'Venerable one, I wish to lodge here, having come on my elder's business. Tomorrow at dawn I shall go to the western quarter, the quarter of Varuna.'
entries.65.5: Hearing Shatrughna's words, that bull among sages laughed and answered that great-souled one: 'You are welcome, greatly renowned one.
entries.65.6: 'This hermitage is your own, gentle one, and belongs to the line of the Raghus. Take without hesitation the seat and the water for feet and hands that I give.'
entries.65.7: Then, receiving that honour and a meal of fruit and root, Kakutstha ate and was fully satisfied.
entries.65.8: And having eaten of fruit and root, he asked that great sage: 'Whose is this glory of sacrifice near your hermitage?'
entries.65.9: Hearing his words, Valmiki said: 'Hear, Shatrughna, whose place this was of old.
entries.65.10: 'There was a king of your forefathers named Saudasa; and that lord of earth had a son named Virasaha, valiant and most righteous.
entries.65.11: 'While he was still a boy, that Saudasa took to hunting; and that brave one saw two rakshasas roaming there,
entries.65.12: 'dreadful ones in the form of tigers, devouring deer by many thousands, and yet unsatisfied and never coming to their fill.
entries.65.13: 'Seeing those two rakshasas and the forest emptied of deer, he was seized with a great anger and slew one of them with a great arrow.
entries.65.14: 'Having brought down that one, Saudasa, bull among men, free of fever and of distress, stood looking at the slain rakshasa.
entries.65.15: 'And the companion of that rakshasa, seeing him standing so, showed a dreadful grief and said to Saudasa:
entries.65.16: '"Since you have slain my companion who had done no wrong, therefore, most sinful one, I shall render you a return for it."
entries.65.17: 'Having spoken thus, that rakshasa vanished upon the spot. And by the turning of time that king came to be called Mitrasaha.
entries.65.18: 'And that king performed a sacrifice near this hermitage — the great sacrifice of the horse, which Vasishtha conducted.
entries.65.19: 'And a great sacrifice it was there, lasting many thousands of years, rich in the highest fortune and like a sacrifice of the gods.
entries.65.20: 'Then at the end of the sacrifice, remembering the old enmity, that rakshasa in Vasishtha's form said this to the king:
entries.65.21: '"The end of this sacrifice has come. Let food with flesh be given me here at once; and let there be no debating it."
entries.65.22: 'Hearing that word spoken by the rakshasa in a brahmin's form, the lord of earth said to his cook, who was skilled in preparing food:
entries.65.23: '"Make ready swiftly a dish of offering-food with flesh, and let it be sweet, so that the teacher may be well pleased."
entries.65.24: 'At that command of the lord of kings the cook was troubled in mind; and then that rakshasa took on the cook's shape there.
entries.65.25: 'And he offered human flesh to the king, saying, "Here is brought sweet offering-food with flesh."
entries.65.26: 'And with his wife Madayanti the king offered that food to Vasishtha, tiger among men — that food with flesh brought by the rakshasa.
entries.65.27: 'And knowing that flesh which had come into the vessel to be human, that brahmin, seized with a great anger, began to speak:
entries.65.28: '"Since you have wished to give me this for food, king, therefore this shall be your food; there is no doubt of it."
entries.65.29: 'Then Saudasa in anger took water in his hand and made to curse Vasishtha; but his wife held him back.
entries.65.30: '"King, since the venerable sage Vasishtha is our master, you cannot curse in return a household priest who is the equal of a god."
entries.65.31: 'Then that soul of dharma let fall that water of wrath, charged with splendour and strength, and wetted his own feet with it.
entries.65.32: 'And by that the king's two feet became mottled; and from that day the king Saudasa of great renown became Kalmashapada, and was so known.
entries.65.33: 'And that king with his wife bowed again and again and told Vasishtha what had been said by the rakshasa in a brahmin's form.
entries.65.34: 'Hearing that from the lord of kings, and the rakshasa's deceit, Vasishtha said again to that king, bull among men:
entries.65.35: '"This word which was spoken by me in wrath cannot be made void; yet I shall give you a boon.
entries.65.36: '"A time of twelve years shall be the end of the curse; and by my favour, lord of kings, you shall not remember what has passed."
entries.65.37: 'So that king, slayer of foes, having borne that curse, won back his kingdom and guarded his people.
entries.65.38: 'That fair place of sacrifice near this hermitage, about which you ask me, Raghava, belonged to that Kalmashapada.'
entries.65.39: Hearing that most dreadful tale of the lord of kings, he saluted the great sage and went into the leaf-hut.
entries.66.1: On that very night when Shatrughna lodged in the leaf-hut, on that same night Sita gave birth to two boys.
entries.66.2: Then at midnight the young sons of the sages told Valmiki the glad news of Sita's fair delivery:
entries.66.3: 'Venerable one, that wife of Rama has borne two boys. Make now, one of great splendour, a rite of protection to destroy hostile spirits.'
entries.66.4: Hearing their words, the great sage came; and the two, of great might, were like the young moon and like sons of the gods.
entries.66.5: He went there with a glad heart and looked upon the boys, and made for them a protection that destroys spirits and rakshasas.
entries.66.6: Taking a handful of kusha grass and some lava grass, that twice-born Valmiki gave them a protection that destroys evil spirits.
entries.66.7: He who was the elder born of the two was to be brushed with the kusha grass hallowed by mantras; and so his name was Kusha.
entries.66.8: And he who was the younger of the two was to be brushed with lava by the old women, with full attention; and so his name was Lava.
entries.66.9: 'Thus these two twins shall be known by the names Kusha and Lava, and shall be renowned by the names I have given them.'
entries.66.10: And those women took that protection from the sage's hand with full attention, and free of fault they performed the rite of protection for the two.
entries.66.11: And so, as that rite was performed by the old women, and their birth and their naming, and the praising of Rama, and Sita's fair delivery of the two —
entries.66.12: at midnight Shatrughna heard that great and joyful news; and going to the leaf-hut he said, 'Mother, by good fortune!'
entries.66.13: And so for that glad and great-souled Shatrughna of swift valour the rainy night of Shravana passed away.
entries.66.14: At dawn that one of great might performed the rites of the forenoon and, taking leave of the sage with joined palms, went on again with his face to the west.
entries.66.15: And going to the bank of the Yamuna and halting seven nights upon the road, he came to lodge in the hermitage of sages of holy fame.
entries.66.16: And there that king of great renown passed the time in fitting talk with the sages, with Bhargava at their head.
entries.66.17: And that great-souled hero of the Raghus, son of a king, together with those sages of golden splendour, brought that night to its end with talk of many kinds.
entries.67.1: Then when night had come on, Shatrughna asked the brahmin Chyavana, the delight of Bhrigu's line, about Lavana's strength:
entries.67.2: 'And of the strength of the trident, brahmin — who were destroyed by it before, coming to single combat with that foremost of tridents?'
entries.67.3: Hearing those words of the great-souled Shatrughna, Chyavana of great splendour answered the delight of the Raghus:
entries.67.4: 'Countless are his deeds, delight of the Raghus. Hear from me what befell one born in the line of the Ikshvakus.
entries.67.5: 'Long ago in Ayodhya there was a mighty king, the son of Yuvanashva, renowned in the three worlds as Mandhatri, endowed with valour.
entries.67.6: 'Having brought the whole earth under his rule, that lord of earth made preparation to go from here and conquer the world of the gods.
entries.67.7: 'And a keen fear came upon Indra and upon the great-souled gods, when Mandhatri made ready with the desire of conquering the world of the gods.
entries.67.8: 'Being honoured by the hosts of the gods with half of Shakra's throne and half of his kingdom, that king still held to his vow.
entries.67.9: 'Knowing that sinful purpose of his, the chastiser of Paka said this, putting conciliation first, to the son of Yuvanashva:
entries.67.10: '"You are not yet king over the world of men, bull among men; and without making the earth subject to you, you desire the kingdom of the gods here.
entries.67.11: '"If, hero, the whole earth entire were yours, then make the kingdom of the gods your own, with your servants and your forces and your mounts."
entries.67.12: 'To Indra speaking thus Mandhatri said: "Where, Shakra, is my rule opposed upon the face of the earth?"
entries.67.13: 'And the thousand-eyed one said to him: "There is a rakshasa named Lavana, the son of Madhu, in the wood of Madhu; he does not obey your command, sinless one."
entries.67.14: 'Hearing that dreadful and unwelcome word spoken by the thousand-eyed one, the king was ashamed and, with his face bent down, could not speak.
entries.67.15: 'Taking leave of the thousand-eyed one, with his face somewhat bent in shame, that glorious lord of men came back again to this world.
entries.67.16: 'And carrying that indignation in his heart, that subduer of foes came with his servants and forces and mounts to bring the son of Madhu beneath his sway.
entries.67.17: 'And that bull among men, longing for battle with Lavana, sent a messenger into Lavana's presence.
entries.67.18: 'And going there he spoke many unwelcome words to the son of Madhu; and even as that messenger was speaking, the rakshasa devoured him.
entries.67.19: 'And when the messenger did not return, the king in anger tormented that rakshasa with a rain of arrows on every side.
entries.67.20: 'Then that rakshasa laughed and took up the trident in his hand, and loosed that finest of weapons for his destruction and his followers'.
entries.67.21: 'And that blazing trident, having burnt that king to ashes with his servants and forces and mounts, came again to Lavana's hand.
entries.67.22: 'So that mighty king was slain with his forces and his mounts. And the power of that trident, gentle one, is beyond measure and beyond compare.
entries.67.23: 'Yet tomorrow at dawn you shall slay Lavana, and of that there is no doubt, while he has not taken his weapon. Your victory is certain.
entries.67.24: 'And there shall be good fortune for the worlds when that deed is done by you. All this has been told you of the evil-souled Lavana,
entries.67.25: 'and the dreadful and measureless power of the trident, bull among men, and the destruction of Mandhatri which came about through it, king.
entries.67.26: 'Tomorrow at dawn you shall slay Lavana, great-souled one, and of that I have no doubt. He goes out without his trident in search of flesh; your victory shall be certain, lord of men.'
entries.68.1: As they told these tales and hoped for a fair victory, the night passed swiftly for the great-souled Shatrughna.
entries.68.2: Then in the clear dawn, at that hour, that bold rakshasa went out from the city, driven by the need of food.
entries.68.3: At that moment the hero Shatrughna crossed the river Yamuna and stood at the gate of Madhu's city with his bow in hand.
entries.68.4: Then at midday that rakshasa of cruel deeds came, carrying a burden of many thousands of living creatures.
entries.68.5: And he saw Shatrughna standing at the gate bearing his weapon; and the rakshasa said to him, 'What will you do with this?
entries.68.6: 'Thousands of such as you, with their weapons, have been devoured by me in my fury, basest of men. Do you look for your hour?
entries.68.7: 'And my food is complete already, basest of men. How have you come today and entered my mouth of your own accord, fool?'
entries.68.8: As he spoke so and laughed again and again, Shatrughna, endowed with valour, let fall tears of rage.
entries.68.9: And from all the limbs of that great-souled Shatrughna, overcome with fury, rays of splendour broke forth.
entries.68.10: And in great wrath Shatrughna said to that night-ranger: 'I wish to fight with you in single combat, evil-minded one.
entries.68.11: 'I am the son of Dasharatha and the brother of the wise Rama — Shatrughna, ever the slayer of foes, come seeking your death.
entries.68.12: 'Give single combat to me who desire the fight. You are the enemy of all beings, and you shall not go from me alive.'
entries.68.13: As he spoke thus, the rakshasa answered that best of men, as it were laughing: 'By good fortune you have come, fool.
entries.68.14: 'The brother of my mother's sister was Ravana, lord of rakshasas; and he was slain by Rama for a woman's sake, evil-minded one, basest of men.
entries.68.15: 'And all that destruction of Ravana's line I bore, setting contempt before me — and you above all.
entries.68.16: 'And all of them have been slain by me and scorned as grass — those that were and those that shall be, and you too, basest of men.
entries.68.17: 'To you who desire battle I shall give battle, fool. Stand a moment while I fetch my weapon; and I shall make ready such a weapon as you would wish.'
entries.68.18: And Shatrughna said to him at once: 'Where will you go from me alive? An enemy seen by chance is not to be let go by one of resolve.
entries.68.19: 'For he who out of a wavering mind gives his enemy room is slain for his dullness of wit, like a coward.
entries.68.20: 'Therefore look well upon the world of the living. With sharp and various arrows I shall send you toward the house of Yama — you who are sinful, the enemy of the three worlds and of Raghava.'
entries.69.1: Hearing that word of the great-souled Shatrughna, he took on a fierce anger and cried, 'Stand, stand!'
entries.69.2: Grinding hand against hand and gnashing his teeth, Lavana challenged that tiger of the Raghus again and again.
entries.69.3: And Shatrughna, slayer of the gods' enemies, said this to Lavana, dreadful to look upon, as he spoke so:
entries.69.4: 'Shatrughna is not born such as those others whom you have conquered. Struck down today by my arrows, go to the abode of Yama.
entries.69.5: 'Let the sages see you slain by me in battle today, evil-souled one; let the learned brahmins see it, as the thirty saw Ravana.
entries.69.6: 'When you are burnt by my arrows and fallen today, night-ranger, there shall be safety in the city and in the countryside.
entries.69.7: 'Today an arrow with a thunderbolt face, loosed from my arm, shall enter your heart as the sun's ray enters a lotus.'
entries.69.8: Being addressed thus, Lavana in a swoon of anger hurled a great tree at Shatrughna's breast; and he cut it into a hundred pieces.
entries.69.9: Seeing that stroke fruitless, that mighty rakshasa took up many trees again and hurled them at Shatrughna.
entries.69.10: And Shatrughna, full of splendour, cut down those many trees as they came, each with three or four smooth-jointed arrows.
entries.69.11: Then Shatrughna, endowed with valour, loosed a rain of arrows upon the rakshasa's breast; yet the rakshasa was not shaken.
entries.69.12: Then Lavana laughed and, raising a tree in his might, struck that hero upon the head; and his limbs slackened and he swooned away.
entries.69.13: And when that hero fell there arose a great cry of woe from the sages and the hosts of gods, from the gandharvas and apsaras.
entries.69.14: And the rakshasa, taking Shatrughna for dead and fallen upon the ground, did not use the opening he had, nor enter his own dwelling.
entries.69.15: Nor did he take up the trident, seeing him fallen upon the earth. Thinking him slain, he carried in those provisions of his.
entries.69.16: And in a moment Shatrughna came to his senses and stood again with his weapon in hand at the city gate, honoured by the sages.
entries.69.17: Then he took up that divine and unfailing finest of arrows, blazing with splendour, dreadful, filling the ten quarters —
entries.69.18: with a thunderbolt face and the speed of the thunderbolt, like Meru and Mandara, smooth at every joint, unconquered in every battle,
entries.69.19: its shaft smeared as with blood and sandal, fair-feathered and winged, the render of the lords of danavas and of mountains and of asuras.
entries.69.20: Seeing it blazing like the fire of Kala when the ending of an age has come, all beings were seized with terror.
entries.69.21: And the whole world, with gods and asuras and gandharvas, with sages and the hosts of apsaras, being unwell, came before the Grandsire
entries.69.22: and said to that lord of the gods of gods, the giver of boons, the great-grandsire: 'There is a bewilderment of fear among the gods, and it points to the destruction of the worlds.
entries.69.23: 'Nothing such as this has been seen or heard before, great-grandsire — this bewilderment of fear among the gods, pointing to the destruction of the worlds.'
entries.69.24: Hearing those words of theirs, Brahma the grandsire of the worlds, the giver of safety to the worlds, declared the cause of their fear and said in sweet words: 'Hear me, all you gods.
entries.69.25: 'It is the arrow held by Shatrughna for the slaying of Lavana in battle. By its splendour we are all bewildered, best of the gods.
entries.69.26: 'This is the eternal arrow of splendour of that first god, the maker of the worlds, my children, from which this fear has come.
entries.69.27: 'This great arrow was created by that great one for the sake of Kaitabha and of Madhu, for the slaying of those two daityas.
entries.69.28: 'Vishnu alone knows this arrow of splendour; it is the former body of that great-souled Vishnu himself.
entries.69.29: 'Go from here and see Lavana, best of rakshasas, being slain by that great-souled and heroic younger brother of Rama.'
entries.69.30: Hearing the words of that god of gods, the gods went to where those two, Shatrughna and Lavana, were fighting.
entries.69.31: And all beings saw that arrow of divine seeming, held in Shatrughna's hand, risen like the fire at the ending of an age.
entries.69.32: Seeing the sky filled with the gods, the delight of the Raghus uttered a mighty lion's roar and looked again upon his mark.
entries.69.33: And being challenged again by the great-souled Shatrughna, Lavana, filled with anger, came forward for the fight.
entries.69.34: And that best of bowmen, drawing his bow to the ear, loosed that great arrow into Lavana's broad breast.
entries.69.35: And tearing his breast open it went swiftly down into the nether world.
entries.69.36: And having gone to the nether world, that divine arrow, honoured of the gods, came back swiftly again to the delight of the Ikshvaku line.
entries.69.37: And Lavana the night-ranger, torn through by Shatrughna's arrow, fell suddenly upon the ground like a mountain struck by the thunderbolt.
entries.69.38: And when that rakshasa Lavana was slain, that great trident, before the eyes of all the gods, passed under Rudra's sway.
entries.69.39: Having brought down with a single arrow one who was a burden even to the three worlds, that hero of the Raghus shone forth with his fine bow and arrow, like the thousand-rayed one when he has driven away the darkness.
entries.69.40: Then the gods and sages and serpents and all the apsaras honoured him: 'By good fortune the son of Dasharatha has won the victory, and fear is cast off and is quiet, like a serpent grown calm.'
entries.70.1: When Lavana was slain, the gods with Indra and with Agni at their head said in sweetest words to Shatrughna, scorcher of foes:
entries.70.2: 'By good fortune the victory is yours, my child; by good fortune the rakshasa Lavana is slain. Choose a boon, tiger among men, holder of good vows.
entries.70.3: 'We are all come together as givers of boons, mighty-armed one, desiring your victory; and the sight of us is not in vain.'
entries.70.4: Hearing the gods' words, that brave and mighty-armed Shatrughna of composed spirit set his palms upon his head and answered:
entries.70.5: 'Let this lovely city of Madhu, Mathura, made by the gods, swiftly be settled with people; let this be my highest boon.'
entries.70.6: And the gods with pleased minds said to Raghava, 'So be it. This lovely city shall be Shurasena, and there is no doubt of it.'
entries.70.7: Having spoken thus, those great-souled ones went up to heaven; and Shatrughna of great splendour brought up his army.
entries.70.8: And that army came swiftly, hearing Shatrughna's command; and Shatrughna began the founding of the city in the month of Shravana.
entries.70.9: And in the twelfth fair year that city of divine seeming was settled, and the country of the Shurasenas had nothing to fear from any quarter.
entries.70.10: The fields stood full of grain and Vasava sent rain in season; the men were free of disease and brave, guarded by Shatrughna's arms.
entries.70.11: Shaped like a half-moon, adorned upon the Yamuna's bank, adorned with fine houses and with crossroads and markets and streets, filled with the four orders and adorned with trade of many kinds.
entries.70.12: And that fair and great work which Lavana had made before, Shatrughna adorned and made lovely with colours of many kinds.
entries.70.13: It shone on every side with pleasure-gardens and places of retreat, and was adorned with other fair works divine and human.
entries.70.14: That city of divine seeming, adorned with wares of many kinds and with merchants come from many lands,
entries.70.15: that flourishing city Shatrughna, the younger brother of Bharata, rich in fortune, looked upon with the highest pleasure and came to the greatest joy.
entries.70.16: And this thought arose in him: 'Having settled the city of Mathura, I shall look upon Rama's feet now that the twelfth year has come.'
entries.70.17: Then, having settled that city like the city of the immortals, thronged with people of many kinds, that lord of men, increaser of the line of the Raghus, set his mind upon seeing the feet of the lord of the Raghus.
